name: MathlibAnnex.SeminormBall.map_eq
title: Equality of seminorm balls under a linear bijection preserves the seminorms

content.display_title: Equality of seminorm balls under a linear bijection preserves the seminorms
content.one_sentence_role: Turns a ball-image equality into one seminorm inequality in each direction.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $E,F$ be real vector spaces with definite seminorms $p$ and $q$, and write $B_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$ and $B_q=\{y:q(y)\le1\}$. If a real-linear bijection $L:E\to F$ satisfies $L(B_p)=B_q$, then

$$q(Lx)=p(x)\qquad(x\in E).$$
content.assumptions: The spaces are real vector spaces. The seminorms satisfy $p(x)=0\Rightarrow x=0$ and $q(y)=0\Rightarrow y=0$. The map $L$ is linear and bijective, and its image of the entire closed seminorm unit ball is exactly $B_q$. No topology, continuity, measure, compactness, finite-dimensionality or volume equality is assumed.
content.conclusion: The given map $L$ preserves the two seminorms pointwise. With ordinary norms this gives the separately stated norm-preservation result for a linear bijection carrying one closed unit ball onto the other.
content.proof_summary:
For $x=0$, linearity and the seminorm axioms give equality. Suppose $x\ne0$. Definiteness and nonnegativity give $p(x)>0$. The normalized vector $u=x/p(x)$ satisfies $p(u)=1$, so $u\in B_p$. The forward ball containment gives $L(u)\in B_q$. By linearity and seminorm homogeneity,

$$\frac{q(Lx)}{p(x)}=q(L(x/p(x)))\le1,$$

and multiplying by $p(x)>0$ gives $q(Lx)\le p(x)$. This is the ball-containment lemma, valid for every $x$ after including zero. Since $L$ is bijective and $L(B_p)=B_q$, its inverse carries $B_q$ into $B_p$. Apply the same lemma with $(q,p,L^{-1})$ to $Lx$:

$$p(x)=p(L^{-1}(Lx))\le q(Lx).$$

Together the two inequalities give the desired equality.

proof_steps.text: To verify the inverse containment, let $y\in B_q$. The image equality supplies $u\in B_p$ with $Lu=y$. Injectivity gives $L^{-1}y=u\in B_p$. Thus the reversed ball-containment lemma has all its hypotheses, including definiteness of $q$.

The two applications of the same lemma have opposite directions: $q(Lx)\le p(x)$ and $p(L^{-1}(Lx))\le q(Lx)$. Substitute the inverse identity in the second and apply antisymmetry. No conclusion is drawn from measure equality alone.

content.lean_realization_notes: The auxiliary forward inequality only needs definiteness of the domain seminorm and containment of ball images. In the equality theorem, definiteness of $q$ is used when that same inequality is applied to $L^{-1}$. The argument is algebraic.
